high.title: Over 80 Points/Week Increase, Has the Stock Market Passed the Bottom?
high.summary: The Vietnamese stock market experienced significant volatility after three weeks of steep decline. VN-Index initially continued falling, breaking below 1,600 points due to increased margin liquidation pressure, with numerous stocks hitting floor prices and pessimistic sentiment dominating. However, prospects of cooling Middle East conflicts and domestic fuel price management measures weakened selling pressure, allowing bottom-fishing capital to enter. VN-Index surged over 81 points from its short-term low, closing the week at 1,672.80 points (+1.52%), though still below the 1,700-point resistance zone. VN30 gained 1.31% to 1,821.53 points but hasn't reclaimed the 200-session moving average. Market breadth was positive with 17/21 sectors gaining. This recovery suggests potential bottoming but traders should watch for sustained break above 1,700 resistance and volume confirmation.

high.title: People Rush to Deposit Money in Banks
high.summary: Vietnam's deposit market in March 2026 shows extremely active dynamics with a widespread interest rate increase race. After maintaining low levels for extended periods, interest rates have established new highs, with some banks reaching 9%/year. 6-month and 12-month terms are most favored by banks for attracting deposits. Techcombank launched programs offering up to 8.4%/year for new deposits in March, adding 1%/year to online deposit rates for 3, 6, and 12-month terms. The bank raised its 12-month rate to maximum 7.4%/year from March 27. Sacombank also implemented preferential rates for new counter deposits from March 26. This aggressive deposit rate competition indicates banks' strong liquidity needs and could signal monetary tightening pressures ahead, impacting VND funding costs and potentially bond yields.

high.title: One Bank Prepares to Implement 20% Stock Dividend Distribution
high.summary: Nam A Bank's Board of Directors approved a capital increase plan for 2026, raising charter capital from over VND 17,156 trillion to over VND 22,588 trillion through three stock issuance methods: (1) 20% stock dividend from retained earnings and capital reserves, (2) ESOP program, and (3) private placement. The stock dividend involves issuing 343 million shares (20% ratio) to existing shareholders from retained earnings and supplementary capital reserves, scheduled for Q2/2026 pending SBV and SSC approvals. ESOP will issue 100 million shares, raising charter capital by VND 1,000 trillion to VND 18,156 trillion, completed by Q2-Q3/2026. This significant capital expansion by a mid-tier bank reflects strong profit retention and growth ambitions, potentially positive for banking sector consolidation trends.

medium.title: SJC Gold and Plain Gold Ring Prices Morning March 31
medium.summary: Gold prices remained stable early March 31. SJC, DOJI, Phu Quy and Bao Tin Manh Hai quoted SJC gold at VND 170.8-173.8 million/tael. Previous session saw gold bars rise VND 0.5-1 million/tael with recovery signs after earlier declines.

medium.title: SJC Gold and Plain Gold Ring Prices Morning March 30
medium.summary: Gold prices unchanged early March 30 at major brands around VND 169.8-172.8 million/tael. Global gold experienced volatility last week, falling near $4,130/ounce before recovering to near $4,500/ounce by week-end. Current spot gold around $4,493/ounce, up slightly from previous week.

medium.title: Largest Oil & Gas Company on Stock Exchange Forecast to Earn VND 3,000 Billion in Q1
medium.summary: SSI Research forecasts PV Gas (GAS) Q1/2026 net profit could exceed VND 3,050 billion, up 11% YoY. Dry gas segment expected to drive profits thanks to higher average FO prices and growing electricity demand. Middle East conflict impact on GAS includes both positive and negative factors.

medium.title: Global Oil Prices Exceed $115/Barrel This Morning as Houthi Forces Enter Combat, US Deploys More Troops to Middle East
medium.summary: Oil prices opened higher Sunday as Middle East officials gathered in Islamabad to discuss de-escalation efforts. Brent crude hit $115.73/barrel at market opening, up $3 from Friday's high of $112.57. WTI reached $103.13/barrel. Oil has surged since US-Israel began bombing Iran in late February, with Iran retaliating by closing Hormuz Strait.
